title: Operator Utility Sandbox and Task DSL for Oncall Playbooks
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers frequently run ad-hoc sequences of admin commands during incidents. Existing runbooks are long prose documents; operators copy/paste commands into shells and maintain local helper scripts. This leads to inconsistent actions, missing telemetry, and difficulty enforcing safety checks.

Goal: Build an interactive Operator Utility Sandbox combined with a lightweight Task DSL (domain-specific language) to author runbooks as executable, reviewable tasks. The sandbox should be safe (read-only by default where possible), provide instrumentation/telemetry for every executed step, support dry-run mode, and integrate with the existing runbook registry and alerts.

Scope: 1) Task DSL v0: YAML-first syntax to declare steps, inputs, expected outputs, and rollback hooks. 2) Sandbox runner: containerized ephemeral environment with scoped credentials, audit logging, and optional confirmation gates. 3) Integration: link tasks to incident pages, expose task execution traces in the Console traces panel, and record per-step cost/latency for optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can author a runbook as a Task DSL YAML file and save it to the runbook registry via the Console UI or Git-backed storage.
Sandbox runner executes tasks in dry-run and live modes; dry-run simulates steps and returns expected outputs without making destructive changes.
Every task execution creates an immutable trace with step-level logs, user who executed, inputs, and duration visible in the Console traces tab.
Security: runs with scoped ephemeral credentials, adheres to least privilege, and triggers a security review for tasks that require write access to production services.
Rollbacks: task author can declare rollback steps and the runner supports automatic rollback on failure when configured.
Integration done: task links show up on incident pages and are referenced from associated GitHub PRs where relevant.
Performance: typical non-blocking step completes within 2s latency in the sandbox; heavy steps report progress streaming to UI.
Telemetry emits events to metrics/observability pipeline for task start/stop/step-fail and task duration; dashboards created for adoption metrics.
decisions: Prefer YAML-first DSL for readability and lintability; plan to support conversion from existing prose runbooks via a migration helper.
Sandbox will default to dry-run for any step that touches critical systems; explicit opt-in flag required for write operations.
Use existing short-lived AWS/GCP service tokens provisioned by ops-k8s-controller; do not introduce new long-lived credentials.
Trace format will reuse Console spans schema so existing tracing UI can render step-level details without new front-end work.
Rollbacks will be optional and author-declared; auto-rollback enabled only for tasks tagged 'safeguarded' in metadata.
implementation_notes:
Implementation plan: (a) Define DSL schema and JSON schema for validation; (b) Build CLI tool that validates and locally simulates Task YAML; (c) Implement sandbox runner as a Kubernetes Job with admission checks and resource quotas; (d) Wire runner to audit-log ingestion and Console traces; (e) Add UI to register/preview/run tasks from Console and incident pages.

MVP: DSL validation + local CLI simulate + server-side runner that can execute a subset of safe steps (kubectl-read, config lookup, secret-read-allowed) + trace emission. Subsequent iteration: write-capable steps, scheduled runbooks, and canary gating.

Trade-offs: We could prioritize a JS/TS SDK over YAML to enable complex logic, but that increases attack surface and review complexity; YAML keeps authorship accessible to SREs. We will later consider providing a minimal embedded expression language for conditional branching.
tasks: Build sandbox runner helm chart and admission policy (Infra)
Implement trace emitter and Console traces integration (Observability)
Create Console UI flow for registering and running tasks (Frontend)
Write migration script to convert 10 high-frequency prose runbooks into Task DSL (SRE)
User testing with oncall team (Beta cohort)
blockers: Scoped short-lived credential provisioning depends on infra task ENG-271443 (k8s service token manager) - waiting for token API stabilisation
Console traces API needs a minor field added to render step-level metadata (frontend change required)
